Definition: to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin — that is how the LORD names Himself on the mountain, and the psalm asks Him to keep and preserve His people from this generation for ever. The proverb commands me to keep my heart with all diligence, and the psalm calls blessed those who keep His testimonies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe keeping is a two-way street: God keeps mercy for me, and I keep His word and my heart. What He preserves, He preserves for ever, and what I guard is my own heart.
